# P31.7 — Claim re-sightings + dating basis (P31)

- **Semantic id:** `DEEPEN.3` · **Phase:** 31 · **Kind:** ticket · **Tag:** p31-followups · **Wave:** B
- **base_branch:** `devin/p31-6-access-edges-and-hosted-link-materialization` · **Depends on:** P31.3 (the duplicate-claim hook), P31.4 (streaming path), P30.2a (ADR-104 capture dating)
- **Run:** `implement-spec spec=docs/tickets/P31.7__claim-re-sightings.md live_verification=true`
- **Gate status:** engineering. The **storage-budget option follows the operator's answer to design §6 Q5**
  (recommended: at most one re-sighting link per claim per cadence window).
  - **RATIFIED 2026-09-24 (operator, LEDGER § GATE DECISIONS "Round 9 ratification", Q5) — CHANGED from the
    recommendation:** *"I'm not sure we should prematurely optimize the repeat-sighting storage since overall data
    size is small and won't grow much."* Record **EVERY** re-sighting — option (a); **no cadence-window cap** and no
    digest-changed filter. In exchange the ticket **measures actual row growth against the 10 GB Cloud SQL disk**
    (deliverable 5), so the "small and won't grow much" assumption is checked, not assumed. *(Disk-size note: the
    ratification says "10 GB"; ADR-107 records `sig-pg` at **15 GB PD-SSD**. The ticket reads the actual provisioned
    disk size read-only and measures against that, reporting the 10 GB figure as well so the stricter bound is shown.)*

## Goal
When a connector re-asserts an unchanged value, record that it was seen again (a `claim_evidence` link to the new
capture, with +0 claims), and make the resolver's capture-dating basis a recorded decision, so reverting values and
restated values are dated correctly.

## Load (cite; do not copy)
- `docs/tickets/DEFERRALS.md` row **D-P30.2a-2**. ADR-104 §4 (undated claims dated from capture; `SIG-RECON-008`), the
  P31.3 ADR (duplicate hook). Spec §28 (resolution, `latest_observation_wins`), §16 (claim/evidence).
- Code: `db/src/db/claim_sink.py` (the duplicate path and the P31.3 hook); `db/deploy/claim.sql` + `claim_evidence`;
  `reconcile/src/reconcile/resolve.py` (+ capture-dating readers); `ops/gcp/materialize.sh` (`resolution`).

## In scope — deliverables
1. **Re-sighting links.** Using P31.3's duplicate hook, append a `claim_evidence` row linking the existing claim to the
   new capture, under the budget rule chosen per Q5: (a) every re-sighting; (b) at most one per claim per cadence
   window; or (c) only when the capture content digest changed. **Ratified: (a) every re-sighting, uncapped** (Q5,
   2026-09-24). It stays idempotent: re-running the same capture adds +0 (one link per (claim, capture), never a
   duplicate link).
2. **Dating basis (ADR-R9-RESIGHT).** Decide whether an undated claim is dated from its earliest or its latest capture
   (or keeps the first-seen date and exposes last-seen separately). Implement the decision in the resolver and record
   the basis in `rules_fired`. Measure and accept the `input_digest` churn the change causes.
3. **Tests.** Re-ingesting an unchanged registry adds `claim_evidence` rows and +0 claims. A fixture A → B → A resolves
   to A (latest observation). Every distinct re-sighting capture adds exactly one link (no cap), and re-running the
   same capture adds +0. There is no UPDATE/DELETE.
4. **Hosted.** Deploy the new image to the scheduled jobs **by digest through P31.4's roll mechanism**. There is **no
   roll onto `sig-sched-camreg-batch-05` until the 2026-10-10 replay's outcome is recorded and design §6 Q5 is
   answered**. Every roll comes only after a bounded measurement of link volume per run (projected monthly rows and bytes against the 15 GB disk). Re-run resolution
   (`materialize.sh --apply run resolution`) as a Cloud Run job; re-run +0 on unchanged input; record the envelope delta.
5. **Growth-vs-disk measurement (operator Q5 condition).** Because every re-sighting is recorded uncapped, measure the
   real cost instead of assuming it: read-only, before and after the first rolled cadence runs, record
   `claim_evidence` row count and `pg_total_relation_size` (table + indexes), the whole-database size, and the
   Cloud SQL disk usage against the instance disk (read the provisioned size — ADR-107 records 15 GB; the operator's
   ratification cites 10 GB, so report headroom against both); derive bytes per link and a 12-month projection at the
   observed cadence mix (OSM monthly included). Record it in the run ledger and ADR-R9-RESIGHT. If the projection
   crosses a stated threshold (e.g. 50% of the disk within 12 months), the ADR's `## Revisit trigger` names that
   threshold and a follow-up (cap or digest-changed filter) is recorded as a deferral — the cap is **not** applied
   pre-emptively.

## Out of scope
- Backfilling historical re-sightings (they were never captured as links; honest history starts at the deploy).
- Changing volatility/half-life values (registry work, P31.8).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unchanged re-ingest → `claim_evidence` links added (every re-sighting, uncapped), 0 new claims, +0 on the same capture (real PG) *(deterministic)*.
- [ ] A → B → A resolves to A; the dating basis is recorded in `rules_fired` *(deterministic)*.
- [ ] A bounded hosted measurement of link volume is recorded with a monthly projection; resolution re-run with its delta recorded, +0 on repeat *(live)*.
- [ ] Actual `claim_evidence` row + byte growth is measured against the Cloud SQL disk (provisioned size read live; also vs the operator-cited 10 GB) with a 12-month projection; the threshold is written into ADR-R9-RESIGHT's revisit trigger *(live, read-only)*.
- [ ] ADR-R9-RESIGHT (dating basis, budget, churn) with `## Revisit trigger` + Appendix F row; D-P30.2a-2 → DONE; `make check` + `make test-db` green.

## Cross-cutting invariants
Cited from `docs/tickets/00_MANIFEST.md` and design §5: insert-only spine (links are new rows); content-keyed
idempotency; labelled inference (capture dating is labelled, SIG-RECON-008); digest-pinned job images, never
`:latest`; measure first; re-run +0; no merge/tag/push-main.
